hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-01.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-01.body:
Every $N\le 20$ works: $N=0+N$ for $N\le 9$; $N=9+(N-9)$ for $10\le N\le 18$; $19=11+8$; $20=11+9$.

For $21=a+b$ with $a\le b$ we need $b\ge 11$, and the only palindrome in $[11,21]$ is $11$. Then $a=10$, not a palindrome. So $21$ fails.

**Answer: 21**

hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-03.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-03.body:
$a-1$ and $b-1$ are reciprocals, so $(a-1)(b-1)=1$, i.e. $ab=a+b=:t$. Then $a^2+b^2=t^2-2t=15$, so $(t-5)(t+3)=0$ and $t=5$ (as $a,b>0$). Therefore $a^3+b^3=(a+b)^3-3ab(a+b)=125-75=50$.

**Answer: 50**

hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-04.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-04.body:
Claim: if $2^k\le n<2^{k+1}$ then $f(n)=2^{k+1}-n$. It holds for $n=1$. If $n=2m$ then $f(n)=2(2^{k}-m)=2^{k+1}-n$; if $n=2m+1$ then $f(n)=2(2^k-m)-1=2^{k+1}-n$ (induction, with $2^{k-1}\le m<2^k$).

So $f(x)=19$ means $x=2^{j}-19$ where $2^{j-1}\le x<2^j$, i.e. $2^{j-1}\ge19$, so $j\ge6$. The bound $x\le2019$ gives $2^j\le2038$, so $j\le10$. The solutions are $2^j-19$ for $j=6,\dots,10$, with sum $(2^{11}-2^6)-5\cdot19=1984-95=1889$.

**Answer: 1889**

hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-05.title: Direct computation
hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-05.body:
Let the common ratio of $b$ be $r$, the common difference of $a$ be $d$, $a_1=a$, $b_1=b$. Then $ab=20$, $(a+d)br=19\Rightarrow 20r+bdr=19$, and $(a+2d)br^2=14\Rightarrow (20+2bd)r^2=14\Rightarrow 10r^2+bdr^2=7$. Multiply the first by $r$ and subtract the second: $10r^2=19r-7$, so $(5r-7)(2r-1)=0$ and $r=\frac75$ or $\frac12$.

From the first, $bd=\frac{19}{r}-20$, so $a_4b_4=(20+3bd)r^3=(57/r-40)r^3=r^2(57-40r)$. At $r=\frac12$ this is $\frac14\cdot37=\frac{37}{4}$; at $r=\frac75$ it is $\frac{49}{25}\cdot1=\frac{49}{25}$. The maximum is $\frac{37}4$.

**Answer: $\frac{37}{4}$**

hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-05.title: Recurrence
hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-05.body:
$c_n=a_nb_n=(sn+t)r^n$ satisfies $c_n=2rc_{n-1}-r^2c_{n-2}$. With $n=3$: $14=38r-20r^2$, so $r=\frac75$ or $\frac12$. Then $c_4=2r\cdot14-r^2\cdot19=28r-19r^2$, which is $\frac{37}4$ at $r=\frac12$ and $\frac{49}{25}$ at $r=\frac75$. The maximum is $\frac{37}{4}$.

**Answer: $\frac{37}{4}$**

hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-06.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-06.body:
$r_1\in[0,\sqrt2)$ and $r_1=b\sqrt3-c\sqrt2$ for an integer $c$; $r_2\in[0,\sqrt3)$ and $r_2=a\sqrt2-d\sqrt3$ for an integer $d$. Then $r_1+r_2=(a-c)\sqrt2+(b-d)\sqrt3=\sqrt2$ forces $c=a-1$, $d=b$ (since $\sqrt2,\sqrt3$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb Q$). The bounds become
$$(a-1)\sqrt2\le b\sqrt3<a\sqrt2,$$
and the condition $r_2<\sqrt3$ follows from it. Thus for each positive integer $b$ there is exactly one such $a$ (the interval $[(a-1)\sqrt2,a\sqrt2)$ containing $b\sqrt3$), and $a>b$. We need $a\le20$, i.e. $b\sqrt3<20\sqrt2$, $b<20\sqrt{2/3}\approx16.33$, so $b\le16$. Hence $16$ pairs.

**Answer: 16**

hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-07.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-07.body:
Let $S$ be the sum. Summing the same expression over all six permutations of $(a,b,c)$ (the rest of the summand is symmetric) gives
$$6S=\sum\frac{3(a^2b+a^2c+b^2a+b^2c+c^2a+c^2b)+6abc}{4^{a+b+c}(a+b)(b+c)(c+a)}.$$
Since $(a+b)(b+c)(c+a)=\sum_{sym}a^2b+2abc$, the numerator is $3(a+b)(b+c)(c+a)$, so
$$6S=3\sum\frac1{4^{a+b+c}}=3\left(\sum_{a\ge1}4^{-a}\right)^3=3\cdot\frac1{27}=\frac19.$$
So $S=\frac1{54}$.

**Answer: $\frac1{54}$**

hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-08.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-08.body:
Let $f_0$ be the multiplicative function with $f_0(p^n)=a_n$ for every prime $p$, where $\sum_{i=0}^na_ia_{n-i}=1$ for all $n$ and $a_0=1$. Then $g(x)=\sum a_nx^n$ satisfies $g(x)^2=\frac1{1-x}$, so $g(x)=(1-x)^{-1/2}$ and $a_n=\binom{2n}{n}/4^n$.

The Dirichlet convolution of multiplicative functions is multiplicative, and $f_0*f_0$ equals $1$ on prime powers, hence is the constant function $1$. Also $f_0(1)=1>0$, so by uniqueness $f=f_0$.

Since $2018=2\cdot1009$ with $1009$ prime,
$$f(2018^{2019})=f(2^{2019})f(1009^{2019})=\left(\frac{\binom{4038}{2019}}{4^{2019}}\right)^2=\frac{\binom{4038}{2019}^2}{2^{8076}}.$$

**Answer: $\binom{4038}{2019}^2/2^{8076}$**

hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-09.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-09.body:
Summing all vertex equations gives $2019T=kT$ where $T$ is the sum of all entries, so $k=2019$ unless $T=0$. If $T=0$, sum the equations over one half-cube (a facet): each entry of that half is counted $2018$ times from inside plus the matching vertex of the other half once, giving $2018S+(-S)=kS$, i.e. $k=2017$ unless the half-sum $S=0$. Continuing with halves of halves, the chain of cases yields $k=2019-2j$ for $j=0,1,\dots$ until all sums of edge-adjacent pairs vanish, which gives $k=-2019$. So $k$ is an odd integer in $[-2019,2019]$.

All of these occur: label vertex $(x_1,\dots,x_{2019})\in\{0,1\}^{2019}$ by $a_1^{x_1}\cdots a_{2019}^{x_{2019}}$ with $a_i=\pm1$. This is $(a_1+\dots+a_{2019})$-harmonic, and the sum of the $a_i$ can be any odd value in $[-2019,2019]$.

Hence $\sum|k|=2(1+3+\dots+2019)=2\cdot1010^2=2040200$.

**Answer: 2040200**

hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-10.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2019-algnt-10.body:
The number $a_{n+1}a_n+\sqrt{a_{n+1}^2-1}\sqrt{a_n^2-1}$ is the larger root of $f_n(x)=x^2-2a_{n+1}a_nx+a_n^2+a_{n+1}^2-1$. Since $a_{n+2}$ is the ceiling of this root, $a_n^2+a_{n+1}^2+a_{n+2}^2-2a_na_{n+1}a_{n+2}-1$ is a small nonnegative integer. Here $a_2=12+\lceil\sqrt{120}\rceil=23$ and the value is $9+16+529-2\cdot3\cdot4\cdot23-1=1$.

By induction (Vieta jumping, using that the sequence grows faster than exponentially) one proves $a_{n+3}=2a_{n+1}a_{n+2}-a_n$ and that this invariant stays equal to $1$. For example $a_3=4\cdot23+\lceil\sqrt{7920}\rceil=181=2\cdot4\cdot23-3$.

Using the recurrence, $\frac{a_{n+3}}{a_{n+2}}=2a_{n+1}-\frac{a_n}{a_{n+2}}$, and from $a_{n+2}=2a_na_{n+1}-a_{n-1}$ we get $\frac{a_{n+2}}{a_n}=2a_{n+1}-\frac{a_{n-1}}{a_n}$, hence
$$\frac{a_{n+3}}{a_{n+2}}-\frac{a_{n+2}}{a_n}=-\frac{a_n}{a_{n+2}}+\frac{a_{n-1}}{a_n}.$$
The summand is therefore $\left(\frac{a_{n-1}}{a_n}-\frac{a_n}{a_{n+1}}\right)+\left(\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_{n+3}}-\frac{a_n}{a_{n+2}}\right)$, which telescopes (the terms tend to $0$ rapidly). The leftover terms are $\frac{a_{-1}}{a_0}-\frac{a_0}{a_2}$ where $a_{-1}=2a_0a_1-a_2=24-23=1$: the sum equals $\frac13-\frac3{23}=\frac{14}{69}$.

**Answer: $\frac{14}{69}$**
